title: Accelerators, Precision & Profiling
description: Study cpu-to-gpu transfer bottlenecks, mixed precision and loss scaling, activation checkpointing tradeoffs, and profiling and warmup-aware benchmarks. Each lesson includes a worked example and an applied practice task.

lessons.title: CPU-to-GPU transfer bottlenecks
lessons.description: Break a training step into loading, transfer, forward, backward, and update times. Identify which component limits throughput.
lessons.conceptOverview: GPU speed depends on keeping the accelerator supplied with data. Data decoding, host memory copies, and synchronization may dominate a small forward pass. Pinned host memory and asynchronous transfer can help in suitable pipelines, but require measurement and correct lifetime handling. Benchmark end-to-end steps rather than isolated kernels only.

sections.content: A GPU may be mostly idle while CPU image decoding saturates one worker. Increasing model batch size alone does not remove that data-loading bottleneck.

lessons.title: Mixed precision and loss scaling
lessons.description: Compare a short FP32 baseline with a supported lower-precision run and record throughput, peak memory, and non-finite values.
lessons.conceptOverview: Autocasting selects lower-precision operations where appropriate while retaining safer precision for sensitive operations. FP16 has limited numerical range; loss scaling can preserve small gradients. BF16 has a wider exponent range but fewer mantissa bits than FP32. Precision changes require quality and stability checks as well as speed measurements.

lessons.title: Activation checkpointing tradeoffs
lessons.description: Compare peak memory and examples per second with and without checkpointing for the same model and effective batch.
lessons.conceptOverview: Activation checkpointing discards selected forward intermediates and recomputes them during backward. It reduces activation memory while adding computation. Savings depend on which regions are checkpointed and on other model-state costs. It cannot eliminate memory occupied by parameters or optimizer state.
lessons.whyItMatters: Checkpointing trades recomputation for activation-memory savings.

sections.title: Worked example
sections.content: Checkpointing a memory-heavy block may enable a larger batch, but the extra recomputation can lengthen each step. The useful outcome is throughput under the actual memory limit.

lessons.title: Profiling and warmup-aware benchmarks
lessons.description: Write a benchmark protocol specifying warmup, repeat count, synchronization, and which latency statistic will be reported.
lessons.conceptOverview: Warmup, compilation, allocator state, and asynchronous execution can distort timing. Measure repeated steady-state steps and synchronize appropriately around device timing. Inspect a profile for idle gaps, tiny kernels, transfer stalls, and memory peaks before changing architecture. Report the workload and measurement protocol.
lessons.whyItMatters: Compare equivalent measurement conditions and include end-to-end timing.
